tasks.title: Per-run progress file runs/<run>.json beside the run lock in the per-user state dir: {run, slug, worktree, launched_by, task, done, total, last_handoff, state}; written atomically by the driver at start, each handoff/task change and stop; derived state, never part of the record (r1-fixes D20 spirit); SPEC Driver section first
launched_by: `sofar drive --detach` captures the calling session id (hook-provided env / session registry) and passes it to the driver; absent when launched from a plain terminal

Statusline drive segment and UserPromptSubmit drive line show live runs this session launched, any initiative or worktree, from the progress file only (one stat + small read); own-record runs keep today's path; rust-core statusline parity
Live proof: detach a run on another worktree from a session bound elsewhere; statusline and prompt line track task/done/total and the stop; statusline p50 within its budget (D18)

payload.text: Origin (2026-09-29, operator-confirmed gap): session c13b1727, whose home is r1-fixes on main, detached linked-context runs in ~/IO/sofar-linked-context and its statusline showed none of them. There are two causes. First, the drive-visibility 3.2/3.3 segment reads only the session's own record's latest run. Second, the run's events live in the other worktree's copy (branch-visibility D1), which is 221+ events ahead of main's. The run lock is already machine-wide, so --stop and --await work across worktrees. Only progress never follows. Related: in-session-drive note 2026-09-17 flagged the progress-visibility gap. drive-visibility phases 4 and 6 are blocked on paid work, hence a separate record.

payload.summary: Built drive-reach 1.1 and 1.2. The driver keeps <state base>/runs/<run>.json beside the run lock. It is written at take, each turn head, each handoff and the stop; done moves at handoffs only, because the driver never folds per poll tick. A write failure is one warning, never a stop. `sofar drive` records launched_by from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, else CODEX_THREAD_ID; `--detach` carries it across the clean-env break as SOFAR_DRIVE_LAUNCHED_BY, which driven sessions never inherit. Cursor exports no session id and the session pointer is last-writer-wins, so Cursor-launched runs name no launcher: a D35 gap for 1.3/2.1 to weigh. Full suite: the same 9 failures before and after (timeouts under load, plus digest-cache Rust/TS parity over the live records); in isolation only digest-cache fails.
